findings: fail() clears loading/sourceReady but relies on an eventual native pause event to change paused; a destroyed HLS source does not guarantee that event.

wantsPlay and the intent ref currently ignore error, so delayed playing/waiting events can revive misleading presentation. Scrolling away and back can also start a fresh request without the explicit retry button.
The existing frontend diagnostics bridge accepts a closed five-value UiMark enum, not HLS type/detail data. This batch adds neither a new IPC nor a wider diagnostic enum.
decisions: A fatal failure immediately revokes the playback intent and explicitly sets paused=true, then preserves the existing one-shot cancellation and source teardown.

Error blocks automatic playback, source acquisition and ordinary video/play-button activation. The ordinary play button remains in its stable position but disabled; the visible error overlay's explicit retry is the sole recovery action.
Explicit retry clears the error and creates one new attempt. Do not add automatic retry loops, source-policy relaxation or a second media transport.

Preserve existing generation/post keys, source URL validation, cancellation, preview priority, muted start, manual pause, HLS bounds and GIF behavior. No CSS, native/API, account, media-data, application lifecycle or other agent-owned source changes.
acceptance: A fatal HLS event after playing, without any pause event, immediately shows a disabled play control rather than pause; no loading indicator remains.
Late playing/waiting/manifest/play-Promise events cannot revive the failed player, remove its error or start another source request.
Scroll-away/return, preview revoke/return and ordinary play/video clicks cannot retry a failed attempt.
One explicit retry acquires exactly one fresh source; successful manifest/play resumes normal controls and subsequent manual pause/play reuses that source.
A second fatal failure remains stopped without further acquisition until another explicit retry; cancellation and HLS destruction remain once per attempt.

autostartRepair.state: Implemented one production option autoStartLoad:false; final 36/36 focused tests and typecheck passed
evidence: Installed node_modules/hls.js/package.json version is 1.7.2; src/config.ts:445 defaults autoStartLoad=true.

Hls src/controller/level-controller.ts:387 emits MANIFEST_PARSED before the src/hls.ts:358-363 MANIFEST_LOADED autostart listener calls src/loader/playlist-loader.ts:398 startLoad(). Atsumi then commits sourceReady and its previous effect cleanup calls stopLoad(), followed by its new startLoad(-1).

Hls src/loader/playlist-loader.ts:141-150 destroys and removes pending playlist loaders on stopLoad, and src/controller/base-stream-controller.ts:176-194 aborts current fragments. The restarted request therefore need not be suppressed as an already-running identical URL.

Native x-video protocol uses four immediate-acquisition slots and a blocking fetch/read with a 20-second bound. Browser abort is not linked to that blocking request, so overlapping canceled and replacement requests can retain multiple slots. This establishes a code-level contention possibility, not the observed Tibo failure cause.

Parent actual evidence: Tibo failed on initial timeline playback but explicit retry and preview succeeded. Tibo root cause and any slot-exhaustion contribution remain unconfirmed; no transport-policy change is authorized by this batch.
autostartRepair.decision: Set only autoStartLoad:false in the existing Hls constructor so the current intent effect is the sole start owner. Preserve explicit restart after pause, all timeout/retry limits, generation/source validation, native code and prior error handling.
